I'm working with a nested editor setup where I have a parent editor and a child editor.

*   When a command is dispatched on a child editor that has NestedEditorExtension registered, and the parent editor is NOT currently running an update, the command must synchronously propagate to the parent editor's registered command handlers after the child's own handlers have run.

*   When command propagation is synchronous (parent not updating), dispatchCommand returns the result of the command dispatch to the parent (true if any parent handler returns true).

*   When a command dispatched by a child editor propagates to the parent, the parent's command handler must receive the child editor as its editor argument (not the parent editor), but $getEditor() within the parent handler must return the parent editor.

*   When a command is dispatched on a child editor while the parent editor IS currently running an update, the child's command handlers run synchronously within the current parent update. The return value of dispatchCommand is false (only reflecting the child-side result), and the parent's handlers are NOT called yet at that point.

*   After the parent editor's active update completes, any deferred command propagation from a child editor must trigger the parent's command handlers exactly once.


*   Interface details: Type: Class
Name: NestedEditorExtension
Location: packages/lexical-extension/src/index.ts
Description: An extension that, when registered on a child editor, causes commands dispatched by the child to propagate to the parent editor after the child's own command handlers have run. If the parent editor is currently in the middle of an update when the child dispatches the command, the propagation to the parent is deferred until the parent's update finishes.


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

Here's what I found about Lexical's nested editor command propagation and deferred update behavior:

## Command Propagation to Parent Editors

The behavior you're describing about `NestedEditorExtension`/nested composers propagating commands to the parent editor is a documented issue. When a command is defined by a plugin that isn't registered on the nested editor, the triggerCommandListeners function iterates the active editors, recognises that there's no listener registered for the command on the nested editor, but then sends the command to the parent editor which just inserts the node within the nested editor anyway.

A related consequence is that nested editors inherit all the node types that are registered in its parent, which makes it difficult to limit the functionality of nested editors.

**How command propagation works generally:** Commands can be handled using editor.registerCommand(command, handler, priority), and incoming commands are propagated through all handlers by priority until a handler stops the propagation (in a similar way to event propagation in the browser). A command handler callback can return true to signal to the other listeners that the command has been handled and propagation will be stopped.

## Deferred / Nested Updates

Regarding the deferred update behavior when working across parent and nested editors: Nested updates are very strongly discouraged because they execute in a very unintuitive deferred manner. When a nested update is scheduled, it returns immediately with no effect, and then executes some time after the parent update has returned.

More specifically on ordering and why this exists: Nested updates get queued to the end of the existing update. This ensures they run in a deterministic order and ensures update callbacks fire in the correct order too. This is really important, as early on it was noticed that updates were being run within an update and all sorts of assumptions would break down. Additionally, this is especially important as Lexical handles the batching of updates and typically tries to flush and commit changes async, but can also do this sync too depending on certain heuristics.

## Relevant Internals

In the Lexical source, each editor holds a reference to its parent and to deferred callbacks. The `LexicalEditor` class contains a `_parentEditor` field, along with `_deferred` (an array of callbacks), `_updates`, `_updating` (a boolean), `_listeners`, and `_commands`.

For dispatching within updates: Calling dispatchCommand will implicitly call editor.update to trigger its command listeners if it was not called from inside editor.update.

## Best Practices for Priorities

If you're trying to intercept/handle commands in a nested editor before they reach the parent: It is best practice to use the lowest priority possible, so most commands will be registered with COMMAND_PRIORITY_EDITOR for the default behavior, then commands to override that behavior can be registered with COMMAND_PRIORITY_BEFORE_EDITOR. In modern Lexical apps, typically only the COMMAND_PRIORITY_BEFORE_EDITOR priority is needed since the last-registered-called-first ordering is suitable for almost all use cases.

---

**Summary of the key takeaway:** The command "leaking" from nested editors to the parent editor is a known limitation ([facebook/lexical#2952](https://github.com/facebook/lexical/issues/2952) and [#4451](https://github.com/facebook/lexical/issues/4451)). A common workaround mentioned in the issue is to disable toolbar buttons based on whether the active editor's `_commands` set includes a given command. If you'd like, I can search for more recent updates on how the newer extension-based API (`NestedEditorExtension`) handles command scoping, since these issues predate that API.

I can't reproduce this file verbatim, since that would exceed the 125-character limit on exact quotes. But I can summarize what it contains.

This is a Lexical extension file (MIT-licensed, Meta Platforms) defining a `NestedEditorExtension`. Here's an overview:

**Interface:** `NestedEditorConfig` has two fields — a `$getParentEditor` function returning a `LexicalEditor`, and a boolean `inheritEditableFromParent`.

**Default helper:** `$defaultGetParentEditor()` retrieves the current editor via `$getEditor()`, registers it with `LexicalBuilder.fromEditor(editor)`, and returns it.

**Extension definition** (via `defineExtension`) includes:
- **build:** creates named signals from the `inheritEditableFromParent` config.
- **config:** default values using `safeCast`, with `$getParentEditor` set to the default helper and `inheritEditableFromParent` as `false`.
- **init:** sets `editorConfig.parentEditor` from the config's parent editor, and inherits the theme from the parent's `_config.theme` if none exists.
- **name:** `"@lexical/extension/NestedEditor"`.
- **register:** runs an `effect` that, when a parent editor exists and inheritance is enabled, syncs editability from the parent and registers an editable listener.

**Regarding your specific request:** There is **no** command propagation, `dispatchCommand`, `registerCommand`, or `defer` logic in this file. The only registration-related behavior is `parentEditor.registerEditableListener(...)`, which forwards editability changes to the nested editor via `editor.setEditable.bind(editor)`.

## Summary

I implemented the deferred command-propagation feature for `NestedEditorExtension` by fixing the command-dispatch machinery in Lexical core (`packages/lexical/src/LexicalUpdates.ts`).

### How it works

The `NestedEditorExtension` already establishes the parent/child relationship by setting `editorConfig.parentEditor` in its `init`, which sets `child._parentEditor`. Command propagation to the parent flows through core's `triggerCommandListeners`, so the feature is driven there.

**What existed already** (satisfying requirements 1–3): when the parent is *not* updating, `getEditorsToPropagate` returns `[child, parent]` and the priority-interleaved loop runs child handlers then parent handlers, passing the *child* as the listener's `editor` argument while `updateEditorSync(parent, …)` makes `$getEditor()` return the *parent*, and the parent's return value is propagated back.

**What I fixed** (requirements 4–5): `getEditorsToPropagate` stops walking at an ancestor that is mid-update but still *included* that ancestor as the last entry — so its handlers were running synchronously inside the parent's active update (the exact nodeMap-corruption hazard the code comments warn about). Now `triggerCommandListeners`:

1. Detects when the last editor in the chain is an updating ancestor (not the dispatching editor itself).
2. Runs the remaining (child-side) handlers synchronously and returns their result — `false` in the tested case, so `dispatchCommand` returns `false` and the parent is *not* called yet.
3. Pushes a single callback onto that ancestor's `_deferred` queue, which fires exactly once when the parent's update commits, propagating to the parent (and its own non-updating ancestors) with the original child still passed as the `editor` argument.

I extracted the shared loop into `triggerCommandListenersInEditors(editors, dispatchEditor, …)` so both the synchronous and deferred paths reuse identical listener-invocation logic.

### Verification
- Wrote a temporary scratch test exercising all 5 requirements (sync propagation, editor-arg vs `$getEditor()`, parent-result return, deferred-while-updating via both microtask flush and `{discrete: true}`) — all passed, then removed it.
- Ran the full `lexical`, `lexical-history`, and `lexical-extension` unit suites: **414 tests passed**, including the existing `LexicalNestedComposer` "command listener delegation" test that pins the interleaved-by-priority semantics.
- `tsc --noEmit` passes clean (exit 0).

No test files were modified.
